summary: Iteration 4 — backend + frontend testing for new features: admin user management CRUD, role guards, random/no-repeat name resolution, shared admin worker fleet, worker file endpoints, and builtin pools. Added /app/backend/tests/test_admin_and_names.py (25 tests, all passing) and ran Playwright flows for admin Users page + role-based UI hiding + redirects. 25/25 backend tests pass; all UI flows pass.

minor.issue: No bare /api/tasks endpoint — only /tasks/active, /tasks/scheduled, /tasks/previous, /tasks/download. Frontend works fine since it calls the segmented endpoints, but worth noting that the review spec said 'tasks/*' (so technically passes).

If a regular user is created with usage_limit < members, task creation 400s with 'Usage limit exceeded'. Not a bug, but the user-creation flow defaults to 15000 in UI while API default also 15000 — admin lowering it to a small number can silently break user task creation. Consider a UI hint.

Indian count=40 and English count=20 are tiny pools; for members>40 the cycling logic produces predictable per-block permutations. Tested and works as documented in _resolve_names — not a bug, just a callout.

issues: Reset usage and Delete use window.confirm() native dialogs instead of a styled in-app confirm modal — works but feels inconsistent with the rest of the dark-themed UI.

action_items: (Optional) Replace window.confirm() in AdminUsersPage with a styled confirm modal for parity with the rest of the UI.
(Optional) When admin lowers a user's usage_limit below current usage, surface a warning in the edit modal.
(Optional) Pre-existing observation from iteration_3: task_poller grace branch comment/behaviour mismatch (now resolved to 'failed' in current code — verified during this iteration).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:887-898 admin_delete_user does cascading deletes AFTER the user doc is deleted; if any of the cascade calls fail mid-way, you end up with orphan tasks/workers/name_files. Wrap in try/except + log, or order: cascade first, then user.
server.py:631-663 _resolve_names() uses random.sample which is O(n) on every claim; for NamesIn (11006) this is fast but consider memoizing pool list to avoid re-copying each call.
server.py:945-950 GET /api/worker/NamesIn.txt is public (no auth). Likely intentional (worker fetches without token), but the file leaks 11k Indian names — confirm this is desired exposure.
AdminUsersPage.jsx uses window.confirm() for destructive actions; replace with in-app modal for UX consistency and testability.
TopBar.jsx renders Users/Workers links only when `isAdmin`. Good. The route guard for /workers and /admin/users also redirects non-admin to /dashboard — verified in browser test.
test_credentials: Admin ppandit6926@gmail.com / alok@zoom123 (seeded). Regular users are created on the fly via /api/admin/users with TEST_ prefix and cleaned up by the fixture.
seed_data_creation: Per-test temp_user fixture creates TEST_user_<rand>@example.com / testpass123 and tears it down with DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}. Admin worker (TEST_W_<rand>) is created and torn down by the admin_worker fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/` for the full backend suite (test_backend.py + test_workers.py + test_admin_and_names.py = 67 tests). For UI flows, the admin CRUD modal uses data-testid='new-email-input/new-name-input/new-password-input/new-limit-input/new-role-select/create-user-submit'; edit modal uses edit-* prefix; row testids are user-row-<uid>, edit-<uid>, reset-<uid>, delete-<uid>. window.confirm is the dialog used for reset/delete — use `page.on('dialog', lambda d: asyncio.create_task(d.accept()))` BEFORE clicking. Logout sometimes does not navigate cleanly via the button; safer to call POST /api/auth/logout via fetch then page.goto('/login').
